sanskrit: vidārya mahatīṃ senāṃ tāvakānāṃ nararṣabhaḥ āsasāda rathaṃ śūnyaṃ bhīmasenasya saṃyuge
english: Having cloven the great host of your warriors, that bull among men came upon Bhīmasena's empty chariot in the fray.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā viśokaṃ samare bhīmasenasya sārathim dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja durmanā gatacetanaḥ
english: Beholding Viśoka, Bhīmasena's charioteer, alone amid the battle, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, grew sick at heart and well-nigh swooned away.

sanskrit: apṛcchad bāṣpasaṃruddho nisvanāṃ vācam īrayan mama prāṇaiḥ priyatamaḥ kva bhīma iti duḥkhitaḥ
english: Choked with tears, uttering a faltering voice, he asked in grief: "Where is Bhīma, dearer to me than my own breath?"

sanskrit: viśokas tam uvācedaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ saṃsthāpya mām iha balī pāṇḍaveyaḥ pratāpavān
english: Viśoka, with joined palms, spoke thus to Dhṛṣṭadyumna: "Having stationed me here, the mighty and valiant son of Pāṇḍu

sanskrit: praviṣṭo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām etad balamahārṇavam mām uktvā puruṣavyāghra prītiyuktam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: has plunged into this great ocean that is the host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, O tiger among men, after speaking to me these affectionate words:

sanskrit: pratipālaya māṃ sūta niyamyāśvān muhūrtakam yāvad etān nihanmy āśu ya ime madvadhodyatāḥ
english: 'Wait for me, charioteer, holding back the horses but a moment, while I swiftly slay these who are bent upon my destruction.'

sanskrit: tato dṛṣṭvā gadāhastaṃ pradhāvantaṃ mahābalam sarveṣām eva sainyānāṃ saṃgharṣaḥ samajāyata
english: Then, beholding that mighty one rushing forward with his mace in hand, a fierce clash arose among all the troops alike.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu tumule yuddhe vartamāne bhayānake bhittvā rājan mahāvyūhaṃ praviveśa sakhā tava
english: And while that tumultuous and terrible battle was raging, O king, your friend, cleaving the great array, entered into it."

sanskrit: viśokasya vacaḥ śrutvā dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi pārṣataḥ pratyuvāca tataḥ sūtaṃ raṇamadhye mahābalaḥ
english: Having heard the words of Viśoka, the mighty Dhṛṣṭadyumna, son of Pṛṣata, answered the charioteer there in the midst of the battle:

sanskrit: na hi me vidyate sūta jīvite 'dya prayojanam bhīmasenaṃ raṇe hitvā sneham utsṛjya pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: "There is no purpose for me, charioteer, in living this day, if I forsake Bhīmasena in battle and cast off my love for the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: yadi yāmi vinā bhīmaṃ kiṃ māṃ kṣatraṃ vadiṣyati ekāyanagate bhīme mayi cāvasthite yudhi
english: If I go without Bhīma, what will the warrior-caste say of me—that, when Bhīma had passed onto a single perilous path, I stood idle in the fight?

sanskrit: asvasti tasya kurvanti devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ yaḥ sahāyān parityajya svastimān āvrajed gṛhān
english: The gods, with Agni at their head, work the ruin of that man who, abandoning his comrades, returns safe and sound to his home.

sanskrit: mama bhīmaḥ sakhā caiva saṃbandhī ca mahābalaḥ bhakto 'smān bhaktimāṃś cāhaṃ tam apy ariniṣūdanam
english: Mighty Bhīma is my friend and my kinsman; he is devoted to us, and I too am devoted to him, that slayer of foes.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi yatra yāto vṛkodaraḥ nighnantaṃ mām arīn paśya dānavān iva vāsavam
english: I shall therefore go to that place where Vṛkodara has gone. Behold me slaying the enemy, as Vāsava slew the Dānavas."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato vīro yayau madhyena bhāratīm bhīmasenasya mārgeṣu gadāpramathitair gajaiḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the hero advanced through the midst of the Bhārata host, along Bhīmasena's tracks marked by elephants crushed by his mace.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tato bhīmaṃ dahantaṃ ripuvāhinīm vātaṃ vṛkṣān iva balāt prabhañjantaṃ raṇe nṛpān
english: Then he beheld Bhīma scorching the enemy's army, shattering the kings in battle by main force, as the wind shatters trees.

sanskrit: te hanyamānāḥ samare rathinaḥ sādinas tathā pādātā dantinaś caiva cakrur ārtasvaraṃ mahat
english: Smitten in the battle, the chariot-warriors, the horsemen, the foot-soldiers, and the elephants alike raised a great cry of anguish.

sanskrit: hāhākāraś ca saṃjajñe tava sainyasya māriṣa vadhyato bhīmasenena kṛtinā citrayodhinā
english: And a wail of woe arose, O venerable one, from your army as it was being slaughtered by the skilled Bhīmasena, that fighter of wondrous craft.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtāstrās te sarve parivārya vṛkodaram abhītāḥ samavartanta śastravṛṣṭyā samantataḥ
english: Then all those masters of weapons, surrounding Vṛkodara, fearlessly closed upon him with a shower of missiles from every side.

sanskrit: abhidrutaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaṃ; samantataḥ pāṇḍavaṃ lokavīraiḥ sainyena ghoreṇa susaṃgatena; dṛṣṭvā balī pārṣato bhīmasenam
english: Seeing the foremost of weapon-bearers, the son of Pāṇḍu, beset on every side by the heroes of the world, by that dreadful and well-marshalled host, the mighty son of Pṛṣata came toward Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: athopagacchac charavikṣatāṅgaṃ; padātinaṃ krodhaviṣaṃ vamantam āśvāsayan pārṣato bhīmasenaṃ; gadāhastaṃ kālam ivāntakāle
english: Then the son of Pṛṣata drew near and comforted Bhīmasena—his body torn by arrows, on foot, spewing the venom of his wrath, mace in hand like Death himself at the hour of doom.

sanskrit: niḥśalyam enaṃ ca cakāra tūrṇam; āropayac cātmarathaṃ mahātmā bhṛśaṃ pariṣvajya ca bhīmasenam; āśvāsayām āsa ca śatrumadhye
english: Swiftly the great-souled one drew the darts from his body, mounted him upon his own chariot, and, embracing Bhīmasena warmly, consoled him in the very midst of the foe.

sanskrit: bhrātṝn athopetya tavāpi putras; tasmin vimarde mahati pravṛtte ayaṃ durātmā drupadasya putraḥ; samāgato bhīmasenena sārdham taṃ yāta sarve sahitā nihantuṃ; mā vo ripuḥ prārthayatām anīkam
english: Then, as that great struggle raged, your son went up to his brothers: "This evil-souled son of Drupada has joined with Bhīmasena. Go, all of you together, to slay him; let not the foe make havoc of your ranks."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vākyaṃ tam amṛṣyamāṇā; jyeṣṭhājñayā coditā dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ vadhāya niṣpetur udāyudhās te; yugakṣaye ketavo yadvad ugrāḥ
english: Hearing those words and unable to brook them, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, urged by their eldest brother's command, rushed forth with uplifted weapons to the kill, terrible as baleful comets at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: pragṛhya citrāṇi dhanūṃṣi vīrā; jyānemighoṣaiḥ pravikampayantaḥ śarair avarṣan drupadasya putraṃ; yathāmbudā bhūdharaṃ vārijālaiḥ nihatya tāṃś cāpi śaraiḥ sutīkṣṇair; na vivyathe samare citrayodhī
english: Seizing their painted bows, those heroes, making the earth tremble with the twang of their bowstrings, rained arrows upon the son of Drupada, as rain-clouds drench a mountain with their torrents of water; yet, striking them down with keen shafts, that fighter of wondrous craft was nowise daunted in the battle.

sanskrit: samabhyudīrṇāṃś ca tavātmajāṃs tathā; niśāmya vīrān abhitaḥ sthitān raṇe jighāṃsur ugraṃ drupadātmajo yuvā; pramohanāstraṃ yuyuje mahārathaḥ kruddho bhṛśaṃ tava putreṣu rājan; daityeṣu yadvat samare mahendraḥ
english: Beholding your sons risen up and standing about him in battle, the young son of Drupada, that mighty car-warrior, eager to slay those fierce heroes, fitted the bewildering weapon, the pramohana, sorely wroth against your sons, O king, as great Indra against the Daityas in battle.

sanskrit: tato vyamuhyanta raṇe nṛvīrāḥ; pramohanāstrāhatabuddhisattvāḥ pradudruvuḥ kuravaś caiva sarve; savājināgāḥ sarathāḥ samantāt parītakālān iva naṣṭasaṃjñān; mohopetāṃs tava putrān niśamya
english: Then the heroic warriors were bewildered in the battle, their minds and senses smitten by the pramohana weapon; and all the Kurus, with their horses, elephants, and chariots, fled in every direction—seeing your sons, swooning and stripped of their wits, as though seized by their last hour.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ drupadaṃ tribhir āsādya śarair vivyādha dāruṇaiḥ
english: At that very moment, Droṇa, the foremost of weapon-bearers, fell upon Drupada and pierced him with three cruel arrows.

sanskrit: so 'tividdhas tadā rājan raṇe droṇena pārthivaḥ apāyād drupado rājan pūrvavairam anusmaran
english: Sorely wounded then in the battle by Droṇa, O king, Drupada the lord of earth withdrew, remembering their ancient feud.

sanskrit: jitvā tu drupadaṃ droṇaḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān tasya śaṅkhasvanaṃ śrutvā vitresuḥ sarvasomakāḥ
english: Having vanquished Drupada, the valiant Droṇa blew his conch; and hearing the blast of his conch, all the Somakas trembled.

sanskrit: atha śuśrāva tejasvī droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ pramohanāstreṇa raṇe mohitān ātmajāṃs tava
english: Then the resplendent Droṇa, foremost of weapon-bearers, learned that your sons had been bewildered in the battle by the pramohana weapon.

sanskrit: tato droṇo rājagṛddhī tvarito 'bhiyayau raṇāt tatrāpaśyan maheṣvāso bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca bhīmaṃ ca vicarantau mahāraṇe
english: Then Droṇa, eager for the king's welfare, hastened thither from the field; and there the valiant Bhāradvāja, that mighty archer, beheld Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Bhīma ranging through the great battle.

sanskrit: mohāviṣṭāṃś ca te putrān apaśyat sa mahārathaḥ tataḥ prajñāstram ādāya mohanāstraṃ vyaśātayat
english: And that mighty car-warrior beheld your sons sunk in stupor; then, taking up the prajñā weapon, he dispelled the bewildering weapon.

sanskrit: atha pratyāgataprāṇās tava putrā mahārathāḥ punar yuddhāya samare prayayur bhīmapārṣatau
english: Then your sons, those great car-warriors, their life-breath restored, advanced once more in the battle to fight against Bhīma and the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prāha samāhūya svasainikān gacchantu padavīṃ śaktyā bhīmapārṣatayor yudhi
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, summoning his own troops, said: "Let them go with all their might to follow the path of Bhīma and the son of Pṛṣata in the fight.

sanskrit: saubhadrapramukhā vīrā rathā dvādaśa daṃśitāḥ pravṛttim adhigacchantu na hi śudhyati me manaḥ
english: Let the twelve mailed heroes on their chariots, with the son of Subhadrā at their head, go and learn the tidings, for my heart is ill at ease."

sanskrit: ta evaṃ samanujñātāḥ śūrā vikrāntayodhinaḥ bāḍham ity evam uktvā tu sarve puruṣamāninaḥ madhyaṃdinagate sūrye prayayuḥ sarva eva hi
english: Thus commanded, those brave and dauntless warriors, all of them proud of their manhood, answered "So be it," and, when the sun had reached the meridian, every one of them set forth.

sanskrit: kekayā draupadeyāś ca dhṛṣṭaketuś ca vīryavān abhimanyuṃ puraskṛtya mahatyā senayā vṛtāḥ
english: The Kekayas, the sons of Draupadī, and the valiant Dhṛṣṭaketu, placing Abhimanyu at their head, set forth surrounded by a great host.

sanskrit: te kṛtvā samare vyūhaṃ sūcīmukham ariṃdamāḥ bibhidur dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ tad rathānīkam āhave
english: Those tamers of foes, forming in the battle the needle-mouthed array, broke through that chariot-division of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons in the fray.

sanskrit: tān prayātān maheṣvāsān abhimanyupurogamān bhīmasenabhayāviṣṭā dhṛṣṭadyumnavimohitā
english: As those mighty archers advanced with Abhimanyu at their head, your army—gripped by dread of Bhīmasena and confounded by Dhṛṣṭadyumna—

sanskrit: na saṃdhārayituṃ śaktā tava senā janādhipa madamūrchānvitātmānaṃ pramadevādhvani sthitā
english: was unable to hold its ground, O lord of men; it stood like a woman swooning with drink and bewildered upon the road.

sanskrit: te 'bhiyātā maheṣvāsāḥ suvarṇavikṛtadhvajāḥ parīpsanto 'bhyadhāvanta dhṛṣṭadyumnavṛkodarau
english: Those mighty archers, their banners wrought of gold, advanced and rushed onward, eager to come to the aid of Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: tau ca dṛṣṭvā maheṣvāsān abhimanyupurogamān babhūvatur mudā yuktau nighnantau tava vāhinīm
english: And the two, beholding those mighty archers led by Abhimanyu, were filled with joy as they smote your host.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca sahasāyāntaṃ pāñcālyo gurum ātmanaḥ nāśaṃsata vadhaṃ vīraḥ putrāṇāṃ tava pārṣataḥ
english: But seeing his own teacher suddenly bearing down upon him, the heroic Pāñcāla prince, the son of Pṛṣata, no longer counted on the slaughter of your sons.

sanskrit: tato rathaṃ samāropya kekayasya vṛkodaram abhyadhāvat susaṃkruddho droṇam iṣvastrapāragam
english: Then, having set Vṛkodara upon the chariot of the Kekaya prince, in great wrath he charged against Droṇa, that master of the arts of the bow.

sanskrit: tasyābhipatatas tūrṇaṃ bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān kruddhaś ciccheda bhallena dhanuḥ śatruniṣūdanaḥ
english: As he swiftly bore down, the valiant Bhāradvāja, slayer of foes, in wrath sundered his bow with a broad-headed shaft.

sanskrit: anyāṃś ca śataśo bāṇān preṣayām āsa pārṣate duryodhanahitārthāya bhartṛpiṇḍam anusmaran
english: And he sent forth hundreds of other arrows at the son of Pṛṣata, for the welfare of Duryodhana, mindful of the bread of his lord.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya pārṣataḥ paravīrahā droṇaṃ vivyādha saptatyā rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Then the son of Pṛṣata, slayer of hostile heroes, taking up another bow, pierced Droṇa with seventy gold-feathered, stone-whetted shafts.

sanskrit: tasya droṇaḥ punaś cāpaṃ cicchedāmitrakarśanaḥ hayāṃś ca caturas tūrṇaṃ caturbhiḥ sāyakottamaiḥ
english: Droṇa, tormentor of foes, again clove his bow, and swiftly slew his four horses with four excellent arrows.

sanskrit: vaivasvatakṣayaṃ ghoraṃ preṣayām āsa vīryavān sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena preṣayām āsa mṛtyave
english: That valiant one sent forth a dread shaft of Yama's destroying power, and with a broad-headed arrow dispatched his charioteer to death.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt sa rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya mahārathaḥ āruroha mahābāhur abhimanyor mahāratham
english: Swiftly leaping down from that car whose horses were slain, the mighty-armed great car-warrior mounted upon the great chariot of Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarathanāgāśvā samakampata vāhinī paśyato bhīmasenasya pārṣatasya ca paśyataḥ
english: Then the host, with its chariots, elephants, and horses, was shaken, while Bhīmasena looked on and the son of Pṛṣata looked on.

sanskrit: tat prabhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā droṇenāmitatejasā nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ samastās te mahārathāḥ
english: Seeing that army broken by Droṇa of boundless splendour, all those great car-warriors together were unable to stem its rout.

sanskrit: vadhyamānaṃ tu tat sainyaṃ droṇena niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vyabhramat tatra tatraiva kṣobhyamāṇa ivārṇavaḥ
english: And that army, slaughtered by Droṇa with keen arrows, wandered hither and thither, like the ocean churned into turmoil.

sanskrit: tathā dṛṣṭvā ca tat sainyaṃ jahṛṣe ca balaṃ tava dṛṣṭvācāryaṃ ca saṃkruddhaṃ dahantaṃ ripuvāhinīm cukruśuḥ sarvato yodhāḥ sādhu sādhv iti bhārata
english: Beholding that army thus, your host was filled with joy; and seeing the teacher in his wrath scorching the enemy's array, the warriors cried out on every side, "Well done! Well done!" O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duryodhano rājā mohāt pratyāgatas tadā śaravarṣaiḥ punar bhīmaṃ pratyavārayad acyutam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then King Duryodhana, recovered from his swoon, once more turned back the unwavering Bhīma with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: ekībhūtāḥ punaś caiva tava putrā mahārathāḥ sametya samare bhīmaṃ yodhayām āsur udyatāḥ
english: And your sons, those great car-warriors, banding together once more and closing upon Bhīma in battle, fought him with high resolve.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi samare saṃprāpya svarathaṃ punaḥ samāruhya mahābāhur yayau yena tavātmajaḥ
english: Bhīmasena too, regaining his own chariot in the battle and mounting it again, the mighty-armed one advanced to where your son was.

sanskrit: pragṛhya ca mahāvegaṃ parāsukaraṇaṃ dṛḍham citraṃ śarāsanaṃ saṃkhye śarair vivyādha te sutān
english: And taking up his swift, sturdy, gaily-painted bow, the bringer of death, he pierced your sons with arrows in the fight.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam nārācena sutīkṣṇena bhṛśaṃ marmaṇy atāḍayat
english: Then King Duryodhana struck the mighty Bhīmasena sorely in a vital part with a sharp-pointed iron shaft.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsas tava putreṇa dhanvinā krodhasaṃraktanayano vegenotkṣipya kārmukam
english: Sorely wounded by your bow-wielding son, that mighty archer, his eyes red with wrath, swiftly raised his bow

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ tribhir bāṇair bāhvor urasi cārpayat sa tathābhihato rājā nācalad girirāḍ iva
english: and planted three arrows in Duryodhana's two arms and his breast; yet the king, though so struck, stirred not, like the king of mountains.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā samare kruddhau vinighnantau parasparam duryodhanānujāḥ sarve śūrāḥ saṃtyaktajīvitāḥ
english: Seeing the two, wroth in battle, smiting each other, all the younger brothers of Duryodhana, those heroes, ready to lay down their lives,

sanskrit: saṃsmṛtya mantritaṃ pūrvaṃ nigrahe bhīmakarmaṇaḥ niścayaṃ manasā kṛtvā nigrahītuṃ pracakramuḥ
english: recalling their former counsel for the seizing of him of dread deeds, and resolving it firmly in their minds, set about to take him captive.

sanskrit: tān āpatata evājau bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ pratyudyayau mahārāja gajaḥ pratigajān iva
english: As they bore down upon him in the fray, the mighty Bhīmasena went forth to meet them, O great king, as an elephant meets rival elephants.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ kruddhaś ca tejasvī nārācena samarpayat citrasenaṃ mahārāja tava putraṃ mahāyaśāḥ
english: And in great wrath that splendid and far-famed one smote with an iron shaft Citrasena, your son, O great king.

sanskrit: tathetarāṃs tava sutāṃs tāḍayām āsa bhārata śarair bahuvidhaiḥ saṃkhye rukmapuṅkhaiḥ suvegitaiḥ
english: And likewise he struck your other sons, O Bhārata, in the fight with manifold gold-feathered, swift-speeding arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃsthāpya samare svāny anīkāni sarvaśaḥ abhimanyuprabhṛtayas te dvādaśa mahārathāḥ
english: Then, having marshalled their own ranks on every side in the battle, those twelve great car-warriors led by Abhimanyu,

sanskrit: preṣitā dharmarājena bhīmasenapadānugāḥ pratyudyayur mahārāja tava putrān mahābalān
english: sent by the King of Righteousness and following in Bhīmasena's track, advanced, O great king, to meet your mighty sons.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā rathasthāṃs tāñ śūrān sūryāgnisamatejasaḥ sarvān eva maheṣvāsān bhrājamānāñ śriyā vṛtān
english: Beholding those heroes stationed on their chariots, splendid as the sun and fire, all mighty archers, radiant and clothed in glory,

sanskrit: mahāhave dīpyamānān suvarṇakavacojjvalān tatyajuḥ samare bhīmaṃ tava putrā mahābalāḥ
english: blazing in the great battle and gleaming in their golden mail, your mighty sons let Bhīma be in the fray.

sanskrit: tān nāmṛṣyata kaunteyo jīvamānā gatā iti anvīya ca punaḥ sarvāṃs tava putrān apīḍayat
english: But the son of Kuntī could not brook that they should escape with their lives; pursuing them, he once again harried all your sons.

sanskrit: athābhimanyuṃ samare bhīmasenena saṃgatam pārṣatena ca saṃprekṣya tava sainye mahārathāḥ
english: Then, seeing Abhimanyu in the battle joined with Bhīmasena and the son of Pṛṣata, the great car-warriors in your army—

sanskrit: duryodhanaprabhṛtayaḥ pragṛhītaśarāsanāḥ bhṛśam aśvaiḥ prajavitaiḥ prayayur yatra te rathāḥ
english: Duryodhana and the rest, their bows grasped firm, with their horses urged to great speed, advanced to where those chariots were.

sanskrit: aparāhṇe tato rājan prāvartata mahān raṇaḥ tāvakānāṃ ca balināṃ pareṣāṃ caiva bhārata
english: Then in the afternoon, O king, a great battle broke forth between your mighty warriors and the foe, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: abhimanyur vikarṇasya hayān hatvā mahājavān athainaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ samācinot
english: Abhimanyu, having slain Vikarṇa's swift horses, then covered him with twenty-five small arrows.

sanskrit: hatāśvaṃ ratham utsṛjya vikarṇas tu mahārathaḥ āruroha rathaṃ rājaṃś citrasenasya bhāsvaram
english: Abandoning that car whose horses were slain, Vikarṇa, the great car-warrior, mounted, O king, the shining chariot of Citrasena.

sanskrit: sthitāv ekarathe tau tu bhrātarau kuruvardhanau ārjuniḥ śarajālena chādayām āsa bhārata
english: As the two brothers, those increasers of the Kuru line, stood upon one chariot, the son of Arjuna covered them with a net of arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: durjayo 'tha vikarṇaś ca kārṣṇiṃ pañcabhir āyasaiḥ vivyadhāte na cākampat kārṣṇir merur ivācalaḥ
english: Then Durjaya and Vikarṇa pierced the son of Kṛṣṇa with five iron shafts; yet the son of Kṛṣṇa stirred not, immovable as Meru.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tu samare kekayān pañca māriṣa yodhayām āsa rājendra tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And Duḥśāsana in the battle, O venerable one, fought against the five Kekayas, O lord of kings; and that was as it were a wondrous thing.
